limitations_and_boundaries: The study focuses on the retinogeniculate system; generalizability to other CNS regions is not directly tested.
C1q and C3 KO phenotypes are assessed at specific postnatal ages (P5, P10, P30); earlier or later time points may reveal additional dynamics.
The glaucoma model uses DBA/2J mice; findings may be specific to this strain and elevated IOP-induced glaucoma.
Electrophysiological input counts may underestimate the true number of inputs due to the resolution of graded stimulation.
The mechanism of complement-mediated synapse elimination (phagocytosis vs. lysis) is not directly demonstrated.

research_questions.statement: Does the classical complement cascade mediate developmental CNS synapse elimination?

provenance.text_excerpt: The remarkably similar phenotypes in the C1q and C3 KO mice, along with the presence of C3 cleavage and activation in the developing but not adult rodent brain, provide evidence that activation of the classical complement cascade occurs during normal postnatal CNS development and helps to mediate normal developmental synapse elimination.

claims.statement: C3 is required for developmental synapse elimination in the retinogeniculate pathway, acting downstream of C1q in the classical complement cascade.
